subject: Aurora Health RFP — governance clarifications (NIST / EU AI Act / eval plan)
messages:
From: Laura Simmons <laura.simmons@aurorahealth.com>
To: neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com, procurement@aurorahealth.com
Cc: Dr. Amit Rao <amit.rao@aurorahealth.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Aurora RFP Q&A: Governance / NIST / EU AI Act / eval plan

Hi Neha and team,

Thanks again for the quick turnaround on the RFP submission. We reviewed the materials you uploaded and have a set of clarifying questions so our compliance and clinical risk teams can complete their evaluation. Please see items below; we need written responses by EOD Thursday 3/25 if possible.

1) NIST AI RMF alignment: Can you indicate which specific subcategories of the NIST AI RMF (Identify, Govern, Detect, Respond, Recover) you map to your product controls? A simple matrix (control -> Redwood feature / doc link) would be ideal.

2) EU AI Act classification: For the models you propose (ensemble of open models + Redwood runtime), how do you classify the offering under the EU AI Act? Which obligations would apply (high-risk, limited-risk, etc.) and what concrete mitigations (documentation, human oversight, record keeping) do you provide?

3) Evaluation/regression plan: We require a reproducible regression harness that we can run on model updates. Please provide a short description of your eval pipeline, acceptance criteria for quality regressions, and whether you provide tooling or artifacts (prompt sets, seed corpora, metrics dashboards) that Aurora can run in its environment.

4) Data lineage & residency: We need an architecture diagram showing where customer data touches Redwood services and whether any PII leaves customer-controlled VPCs for the proposed Dedicated deployment.

5) Evidence: Please attach copies of SOC 2 type II, and any third-party penetration test summaries (redacted as necessary).

Attachments: Aurora_RFP_Q1_2027.pdf (RFP sections + redlined requirements)

We appreciate concise, actionable answers and a sample timeline for item 3 if you can provide it. Happy to schedule a 30-minute call later this week.

Regards,
Laura Simmons
Senior Manager, Strategic Procurement
Aurora Health
[Attachment: Aurora_RFP_Q1_2027.pdf (application/pdf)]

Subject: Re: Aurora RFP Q&A: Governance / NIST / EU AI Act / eval plan

Hi Laura — thanks for the clear questions and the timeline.

Short summary up front: we can provide a NIST control mapping matrix, a position statement on EU AI Act classification (including recommended contractual commitments), a reproducible eval/regression harness (Dockerized runner + seed artifacts), an architecture/data-flow diagram for Dedicated/VPC options, and copies of SOC 2 Type II. See details below and attached timeline.

Answers at a glance:
- NIST mapping: we map controls primarily under Identify (asset inventory, model inventory), Govern (policy enforcement, access controls), Detect/Respond (anomaly detection, tracing hooks), and Recover (backup config + failover policies). We'll provide a one-page matrix per your request.
- EU AI Act: our standard Hosted offering would be "limited-risk" for assistive models in X scenarios, but when used for clinical decision support the combination of model + intent could classify as high-risk. For Dedicated/VPC deployments we recommend contractual attestations and joint-risk-assessments; Redwood provides human oversight tooling, logging (immutable audit trails), and record-keeping exports to satisfy key obligations.
- Eval/regression: we supply a reproducible harness (containerized runner + versioned prompt sets + metrics package). Acceptance criteria are configurable per customer; default alerting thresholds are <=2% regression on primary QA metrics (BLEU/ROUGE/semantics) or customer-defined golden prompts.
- Data residency: Dedicated deploy keeps customer data in their VPC; in Hosted mode telemetry and aggregated metrics are stored in our US regions by default (we can enable EU-only regions).
- Evidence: SOC 2 Type II available (we will attach). Pen test summaries can be redacted.

Proposed next steps:
1) I'll consolidate a short deliverables packet by EOD Wednesday 3/24 and share attachments.
2) Can we schedule 30 minutes on Thursday 3/25 at 10am ET for a walkthrough? Please confirm.

Attaching a preliminary timeline and a placeholder NDA we can sign.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Director, Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com

Neha / team — draft plan below. I'm keeping it concise for the customer packet; happy to expand if Aurora asks for more detail.

Evaluator harness (summary):
- Delivery: Docker image (redwood/eval-runner:202703) + README + versioned prompt sets (CSV) + canonical seed corpus (anonymized) stored in Drive.
- Metrics: default: semantic-similarity (embedding cosine), top-k accuracy on golden labels, safety classifiers (to detect hallucination/toxicity), latency percentiles. Each metric has a semantic threshold and a guardrail threshold.
- Regression policy: when a new model baseline is built, we run the runner against the golden prompt set and compute delta; alerts trigger if primary metric delta exceeds 2% absolute or guardrail metric crosses threshold.
- Reproducibility: runner pins model hash, seed RNG, and dataset version; artifacts include a JSON results bundle and an HTML dashboard export.
- Customer-run option: we can provide the Docker image and prompt artifacts to Aurora to run in their environment (Dedicated/VPC) and provide a sample runbook.

Timeline (minimal):
- Wed 3/24: deliver packet (NIST matrix, eval summary, dataflow PNG)
- Thu 3/25: 30-min walkthrough call; run through packet and next steps
- Fri 3/26: provide optional sample eval run (short) if Aurora wants a live demo.

Drive links (internal):
- https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcD-Aurora-RFP (contains prompt sets, runner README, draft NIST matrix)

I'll attach a short exemplar README and sample metrics output for the packet.

— Markus
Lead, Applied ML — Redwood Inference
